self_allowance_enabled.meaning: victim has an active self-allowance in the vault established by a validator-signed permit

victim_has_shares.meaning: victim holds shares in the WERC7575Vault covered by the self-allowance

caller_is_owner_or_approved.meaning: the caller of withdraw/redeem is the owner (victim) or an address approved by the owner

assumptions: Enabling a user's self-allowance via a validator-signed permit is part of the normal protocol flow (as_self_allowance_normal_flow).
withdraw() and redeem() are alternative single-call paths for the same unauthorized burn/withdrawal effect.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the attacker must first obtain or trigger the validator-signed permit enabling the victim's self-allowance, or whether it already exists; the plan treats the self-allowance as already active before the call.
Report does not state whether the victim's self-allowance is unlimited or bounded by a specific allowance value, so no numeric allowance bound is encoded.

limitations: Only the direct impact i_burn_victim_shares is formalized; i_assets_sent_to_attacker, i_victim_zero_balance and i_full_drain_single_tx are deferred to future claims.
The authorization predicate caller_is_owner_or_approved is a report-grounded Boolean because the report states the qualitative requirement without a numeric definition.
The condition encodes the general unauthorized-caller scope (caller is not owner and not approved) rather than the concrete attacker/victim configuration.
Code-level binding of spendSelfAllowance and the permit mechanism is deferred.
